purpose: Adds conversation-mode context-window management for @mention threads: per-thread turn tracking with a hard maxTurns auto-close, a sliding message window condensed into LLM-generated summary snapshots via a shared estimateTokens utility, and configurable limits through env vars and a new .opencode-reviewer.yml conversation section.
riskRationale: The core mechanics are sound and well-tested (25 focused unit tests pass, typecheck/lint clean), but thread state is keyed by repo/pr/file, collapsing distinct conversations so turn counts and summaries leak across unrelated threads; the newly documented yml conversation section is validated but never consumed at runtime; in-memory state is never evicted and is mutated non-atomically under concurrent webhooks; a failed summarization pass over-records coverage and silently drops context; and the sliding-window feature never engages for the most common issue-comment mentions because that thread gatherer caps threads at ~6 messages. No security issues found.
breakingChanges: ConversationConfig gained three required fields (maxTurns, slidingWindowSize, contextTokenBudget), so external code constructing a literal ConversationConfig must add them
Threads longer than slidingWindowSize are now trimmed in the conversation prompt (with an omission note) even before a summary snapshot exists

text: A well-structured implementation that follows the codebase's resilience conventions: the shared estimateTokens utility, an auto-close check that runs before spending a model call, careful ordering that reads the main reply before the summarization pass so it cannot be clobbered, best-effort state updates that never fail a turn, and 25 focused unit tests that all pass. However, the feature has design-level gaps that should be addressed before merge: thread-identity collisions that can auto-close unrelated conversations, a documented yml config surface that is wired nowhere, unbounded and unsynchronized in-memory state, failure-path summary bookkeeping that silently drops context, and summarization that never triggers for issue-comment mentions.

reasoning: The core mechanics are correct and well-tested at the pure-function level, but the state-granularity bug, dead yml config, unbounded/unsynchronized state, and failure-path coverage over-recording need design-level fixes before merge; these are not safely auto-fixable by an automated agent.

message: Good DRY extraction: estimateTokens moved to a shared utility and reused by MCP trimming (mcp/client.ts) so both consumers stay aligned on the same ~4-char/token heuristic and cannot drift.

Checking shouldAutoClose before launching a model call is a clean cost guard — closed threads answer with a pre-formatted message instead of burning tokens, and failed runs do not advance the turn count.

Reading the main reply from conversation-output.txt before the summarization pass runs is a correct ordering choice that guarantees the secondary run can never overwrite the primary response; writing the summary to a separate file adds a second layer of safety.

The doubling heuristic for when to re-summarize (older chunk >= 2x covered) bounds summarization cadence so an LLM pass does not run every turn, and state updates are best-effort so the feature degrades gracefully.

25 focused unit tests cover token estimation, sliding-window application, summary-preamble injection, context-usage reporting, warning thresholds, and every ConversationStateManager decision; the full suite passes (930 lib tests) with typecheck and lint clean.

threadId is keyed as `${repo}/${prNumber}/${filePath || 'issue'}`, so ALL issue-level @mentions on a PR share a single ConversationState and every inline review thread on the same file shares another. Turn count, auto-close, and summarySnapshot then bleed across unrelated conversations: after 50 total issue mentions anywhere on the PR every future issue @mention is auto-closed with the same message, and one thread's summary can be injected into a different thread's prompt on the same file. The ConversationState.threadId JSDoc even documents the intent as 'repo+pr+thread-root-id', and the engine fallback conversationThreadId (lib/src/conversation/state.ts:22) also omits the repo, colliding across repos with the same PR number.
suggestion: Include the triggering/root comment id in the threadId for review-comment threads (the handler already has commentId) so each distinct discussion tracks its own turns/summary, and add the repo to the engine fallback key so it is collision-free across repos.

message: The new `conversation:` section added to PromptConfig/PromptConfigSchema/validateConfig and documented in the README is validated but never consumed at runtime. The app builds config exclusively from DEFAULT_CONFIG + env vars (app/src/utils/config.ts:85) and never calls loadConfig/validateConfig; the action builds AgentConfig from `...DEFAULT_CONFIG` and never maps `loadedConfig?.conversation` (action/src/index.ts:187-294). Users who set maxTurns/slidingWindowSize/contextTokenBudget in .opencode-reviewer.yml silently get defaults. Additionally engine.ts:1397 reads this.config.conversation directly, so naively wiring a partial yml section would yield an undefined slidingWindowSize and NaN coverage in shouldSummarize.
suggestion: Wire loadedConfig.conversation into AgentConfig.conversation in action/src/index.ts (and/or load the yml in the app), merging over DEFAULT_CONFIG.conversation, and add a test asserting yml values reach engine.runConversation; otherwise remove the yml section + schema + README example. Have the engine normalize through the shared defaults instead of reading the config directly.

message: gatherIssueCommentThread truncates issue-level @mention threads to the trigger plus the 5 preceding comments (~6 messages max), always below the default slidingWindowSize of 20, so shouldSummarize never fires and the sliding-window/summarization machinery — the headline feature — is dead for the most common non-inline mention flow. Only turn-count auto-close applies, and because of the coarse threadId that count is shared across all issue mentions on the PR.
suggestion: Accumulate issue comments up to the configured slidingWindowSize (or token budget) so the sliding window can actually engage, and fix the threadId granularity so each conversation is tracked independently; otherwise document explicitly that sliding-window summarization only applies to review-comment threads.

message: When summarizeOlderMessages fails (run failure, timeout, or empty/stale conversation-summary.txt), it returns the previous snapshot or '' but runConversation still calls updateState with summarizedCount = threadLength - slidingWindowSize. The state now claims the whole older chunk is covered when it wasn't, so messages between the old and new coverage are dropped from the window and never condensed. The fixed summary file is also never unlinked before the run, so a successful run that writes nothing silently reuses the previous turn's file content as a 'fresh' snapshot.
suggestion: Only advance summarizedCount when a genuinely fresh summary was produced — have summarizeOlderMessages signal freshness (e.g. return {text, fresh}) and keep the previous coverage otherwise so shouldSummarize re-triggers next turn — and unlink conversation-summary.txt before launching the run so a failed/empty write yields an empty read and the existing fallback.

message: summarizeOlderMessages slices the ENTIRE older chunk (context.thread.slice(0, splitAt)) and buildConversationSummaryPrompt embeds every message verbatim, while the previous summarySnapshot is never passed in. Each re-summarization re-sends the full history it already condensed, so the summary prompt grows linearly with thread length (up to the 500-comment fetch cap) and can overflow the very context budget this feature protects — the run then fails and falls back to the stale snapshot.
suggestion: Make summarization incremental: pass the existing summarySnapshot plus only the messages added since the last snapshot (olderMessages.slice(state.summarizedCount ?? 0)) and instruct the model to merge, bounding the summary prompt to O(window) instead of O(thread length).

message: ConversationStateManager keeps every thread's state in an in-memory Map that is never pruned, and lastActivityTimestamp/messageCount are written but never read anywhere (lib/src/types/index.ts:443,449). On a long-lived Probot instance every unique repo/pr/file and repo/pr/issue entry accumulates forever — a slow but unbounded memory leak — and the two fields are dead bookkeeping.
suggestion: Add TTL-based eviction keyed on lastActivityTimestamp (e.g. prune states idle > 24h when inserting a new one) and/or cap the Map size, so the tracked fields serve a purpose and memory stays bounded.

message: handleConversation is invoked with tempDir = undefined, so every conversation runs in the shared process.cwd() and writes the same .opencode/conversation-output.txt and — new in this PR — .opencode/conversation-summary.txt. Probot handles webhooks concurrently (app.onAny awaits router.handle per event), so two overlapping conversations can clobber each other's files and one can read/post the other's reply or summary. Meanwhile updateState performs a non-atomic state.turnCount += 1 after the model await, so concurrent turns on the same thread can drop a turn increment or clobber a summary (double-spend / under-count toward auto-close).
suggestion: Give each conversation a per-thread scratch directory (e.g. os.tmpdir()/opencode-conv/<repo>-<pr>-<commentId>) and serialize per-thread state transitions with a mutex keyed by threadId (or increment the turn count up front before the model call).

message: The summarization runOpenCode call is not followed by recordTelemetry, unlike every other model call in the engine, so every summary pass's tokens/cost are invisible to getLastTelemetry and the token/cost exposure added in #306 — underreporting that can silently mask cost runaway on long threads.
suggestion: Record the summarization run via recordTelemetry with the summarization model, mirroring the main conversation call.
suggestionCode:
await this.recordTelemetry(
  context.prContext.number,
  runResult.durationMs,
  runResult.tokensUsed,
  runResult,
  config.summarizationModel ?? this.resolveModel('conversationModel'),
  workDir,
);

message: estimatedTokens is computed from sections.join() before the Warnings and Context Usage footers are appended (pushed at lines 297-314), so the reported 'Context: ~N / budget' undercounts the real prompt by roughly 40-100 tokens and the 90%-budget warning threshold is evaluated against that undercount.
suggestion: Compute estimateTokens after appending the footer/warning sections (just before the final join) so the reported usage matches the real prompt size.

message: summarizationModel is declared on ConversationConfig and consumed at engine.ts:1520, but no env var, yml schema field, or DEFAULT_CONFIG value sets it — it is always undefined in practice and silently falls back to the conversation model, so the advertised model override is dead configuration.
suggestion: Either wire it (add a CONVERSATION_SUMMARIZATION_MODEL env var in app/src/utils/config.ts and a summarizationModel field in the schemas/PromptConfig conversation section) or remove it from the public type until it is reachable.

message: DEFAULT_CONVERSATION_CONFIG (maxTurns 50 / slidingWindowSize 20 / contextTokenBudget 32000) duplicates the same defaults already set in DEFAULT_CONFIG.conversation (lib/src/types/index.ts:1128). Two sources of truth that can drift silently.
suggestion: Export the defaults once (e.g. from types/index.ts / DEFAULT_CONFIG.conversation) and have normalizeConversationConfig import them instead of re-declaring a second literal.

message: After auto-close, every subsequent @mention on the thread returns the identical close message and the handler posts it as a brand-new comment each time — repeated duplicate-comment spam on already-closed threads rather than a one-time notice.
suggestion: Track an 'alreadyClosed' flag on ConversationState and post the close message once, returning a silent no-op (or a short 'this thread is closed' notice) on later mentions.

message: The 25 tests cover only the pure functions (estimateTokens, prompt builders, state manager, threadId helpers). None exercise engine.runConversation orchestration — the auto-close short-circuit before the model call, the response-read-before-summary ordering, state update on model failure, or the summary-fallback path — which is where the trickiest new logic lives, nor is there a test that distinct threadIds get isolated state or that the yml conversation section flows into runtime config.
suggestion: Add engine-level tests (mock runOpenCode / fs) asserting: auto-close returns the close message without invoking the model; a failed summary does not advance summarizedCount; the summary pass runs only when shouldSummarize fires and preserves the previous snapshot on failure; state is isolated per threadId; and a config-roundtrip proves validateConfig -> buildConfig wiring.

message: The JSDoc claims the synchronous summarization pass adds 'negligible' latency, but each pass is a full opencode run over all older messages with the full config timeoutMinutes, blocking the user's reply until it completes — doubling worst-case turn latency and model cost on summary turns.
suggestion: Correct the doc and expose a toggle to disable summarization, or run the summarization best-effort after posting the reply so it does not block the response.
